description: Project-specific registry for formulas, thresholds, scoring rules, heuristics, and constants used by x-tech-hackathon.

entries.expression: For simulation and fixture-backed demos only: 2 PPS selects route_a, 4 PPS selects route_b, and 8 PPS requests return_to_base. Any unmatched, ambiguous, stale, or out-of-context pulse observation is rejected or routed to human review.

variables.observed_pulse_rate_pps: Observed optical cue pulse rate in pulses per second.
variables.route_options: Prevalidated route options available in the current mission state.
variables.mission_state: Current state-machine state and allowed transitions.
variables.cue_context: Observed cue location, timestamp, source, confidence, and expected sector/window.

chosen_for: Keeps the hackathon route-selection interaction simple and easy to explain.
Uses only prevalidated route options and preserves human review for unsafe or ambiguous cases.
rejected_for: Operational drone command without human-approved safety gates.
entries.notes: Pulse-rate mapping is not authentication and can be spoofed or misread. Treat cue observations as intent hints that must be checked against expected sector, time window, state-machine transition, and route safety constraints.

entries.expression: For simulation and fixture-backed demos only: 1 PPS previews hold_or_loiter, 2 PPS previews route_a, 4 PPS previews route_b, and 8 PPS previews or requests return_to_base. Continuous illumination, no pulse, unmatched rates, ambiguous rates, stale observations, or out-of-context observations are rejected or routed to human review.

variables.observed_pulse_rate_pps: Observed optical cue pulse rate in pulses per second.
variables.allowed_commands: Commands permitted in the current mission state.
variables.mission_state: Current state-machine state and allowed transitions.
variables.cue_context: Observed cue location, timestamp, source, confidence, and expected sector/window.
variables.operator_confirmation: Whether a human operator confirmed the previewed command.

chosen_for: Extends the user-provided route mapping into a compact drone command grammar.
Keeps commands limited to ISR/recon planning, route choice, hold/loiter, and RTB.
Separates cue observation from command execution by requiring state validation and operator review.
rejected_for: Operational drone command without human-approved safety gates.
entries.notes: Use this as the preferred v1 command grammar for the hackathon demo. The cue is an intent hint, not proof of friendly identity. All non-RTB commands should be previewed before state-machine advancement; RTB may be visually prioritized but should still be logged and explainable.

entries.expression: For fixture-backed demos, generate terrain attention points inside the buffered unit movement corridor. Mark obstacle_candidate when terrain/context intersects the route corridor or a manual obstacle is present. Mark scout_high_ground when a local high point or ridge candidate is within drone range and can observe an upcoming route segment. Mark coverage_gap when a route segment is outside the planned drone sensor/coverage area. All generated points are planning aids, not authoritative terrain truth.

variables.planning_corridor: Buffered area around the unit route.
variables.manual_features: Operator-drawn obstacles, no-go zones, or scout candidates.
variables.drone_profile: Demo drone endurance, speed band, sensor radius, and hold defaults.
variables.planned_drone_routes: Candidate drone route, hold, and RTB paths.

chosen_for: Keeps terrain analysis explainable and demoable.
Works from deterministic fixtures before external terrain APIs are connected.
Supports the moving-unit drone planning scenario without pretending to be authoritative doctrine.
rejected_for: Unreviewed obstacle avoidance for real drone control.
entries.notes: Use fixture thresholds and manually curated terrain examples for the hackathon. If external DEM data is added, cite the exact source and record any thresholds separately before relying on them.

entries.expression: For fixture-backed planning demos, default drone route branches to 120 meters above terrain level. When terrain elevation is available, compute altitude_msl_m = terrain_elevation_m + 120. If terrain elevation is unavailable, preserve the route but mark altitude planning as degraded and require a visible warning.

variables.terrain_elevation_m: Terrain elevation at the waypoint or route segment sample.
variables.altitude_agl_m: Planned altitude above terrain level for the drone route point.
variables.altitude_msl_m: Computed planned altitude above mean sea level.
variables.terrain_status: Whether terrain data was available and suitable for the route altitude calculation.

chosen_for: Matches user-selected default for the hackathon planning demo.
Keeps route altitude explainable in AGL terms while allowing Cesium to render MSL coordinates.
Provides a simple first pass before editable per-waypoint altitude is implemented.
rejected_for: Real drone autopilot upload or hardware command.
entries.notes: Use 120 m AGL as a provisional default only. Future per-waypoint or per-segment altitude edits should cite this rule as the default fallback and add separate validation for operator overrides.
